finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled `asciitrim` replaces markdown-it's linear native `.trim()` with a backtracking regex that is quadratic on long whitespace runs (redos / stored client-side dos)
evidence: The regex at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-20, applied with `String.replace` at line 22, contains the classic quadratic-trim alternative `[ws]+$`: an unanchored greedy single-char-class loop followed by an end assertion, which in V8 restarts and fully backtracks at every offset of a non-terminal whitespace run (O(k^2)) — the same shape as the known `trim`/`trim-newlines` ReDoS advisories. It is reached from `lheadingRule`'s `asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` (~line 133) on unbounded paragraph text, and preview.ts:`render()` plus editor.ts's `docChanged` updateListener re-run `md.render()` on the whole document for every local keystroke and every remote Yorkie sync, so a stored note can pin a collaborator's main thread. Qualifications that lower severity rather than negate the finding: the path requires an actual setext underline to be recognized, needs tens of thousands of contiguous whitespace chars on one line, and the author must already have write access; I also could not verify (no checkout) that upstream markdown-it uses linear `.trim()` here, though that affects only the "introduced by this change" framing, not the quadratic behavior of the code as written.
